title: Halo POC — recommended shortlist & hands-on eval blueprint
text:
Halo POC — recommended shortlist & hands-on eval blueprint

['From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@haloanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Halo POC — recommended shortlist & hands-on eval blueprint

Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for the demo today. Really appreciated the walkthrough of the ingestion pipeline and the low-latency search use case you showed — that clarified the primary constraints (95th percentile latency target of 150ms, throughput of ~60 reqs/s during peak). Per our conversation, we ran a short rack of tests and are proposing a small, pragmatic shortlist to validate during a 7–10 day hands-on eval.

High-level recommendation (attached eval pack):
- Candidate A (quant-4): best raw cost/perf for batched MMR reranking — expect ~25–40% cost reduction vs baseline with similar pass-rate on relevance tests.
- Candidate B (low-lat, fp16): beats latency SLO at sequence lengths <=512; higher token cost but reduces tail latency risk.
- Candidate C (sparse-KV variant): conservative quality profile, best for long-dialog contexts we saw in your demo.

What we included in the eval pack: prompt set (halo_eval_prompt_set_v1.csv) with 120 representative queries, a lightweight latency & cost matrix (latency_cost_matrix_q2.xlsx), and a mutual action plan template so we can keep the sprint focused. Quick asks from you to get started:
1) Confirm the target test window (7 vs 10 days).
2) Share a short sample of production traffic (anonymized) or confirm we can use the curated prompt set as-is.
3) Point-of-contact for infra access (service account or SSO user).

Next steps we propose:
- Day 0: onboarding + service account access; we deploy candidate variants in sandbox.
- Day 1–3: smoke tests + microbenchmarks (latency curves, token cost).
- Day 4–7(10): regression-quality sweep against prompt set; handoff of evaluation dashboard and suggested final pick.

Ben and Marissa are looped for ops/billing and evaluation guardrails. I’ll hold a 30-min check-in after day 3 to sync on any surprises.

If that plan looks good I’ll send calendar invites and push the eval pack to your Drive link.

Thanks —
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova | Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference — inference for production

Attachments: halo_eval_prompt_set_v1.csv (csv), latency_cost_matrix_q2.xlsx (spreadsheet), mutual_action_plan_halo.docx (docx)', 'From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@haloanalytics.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Halo Analytics Engineering <eng@haloanalytics.com>
Date: 2028-06-04T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Halo POC — recommended shortlist & hands-on eval blueprint

Thanks Sofia — this looks very actionable. A couple quick clarifications:  
- We prefer a 10-day window so we can exercise longer-tail queries (we saw a few long-context threads in the demo).
- I’ll upload a sanitized 1k request sample to the Drive folder you shared by EOD tomorrow.
- Point-of-contact for infra: please use eng@haloanalytics.com; our infra lead is Tomas (tomas@haloanalytics.com) who can create the service account.

One risk callout: if Candidate B is the low-latity option (fp16), we’re concerned about hallucination on certain legal/regulatory prompts. Can you include a quick QA checklist for quality regression tracking? Also we’ll need an explicit summary of cost delta at 95th pct vs median.

Aisha
Aisha Khan | Product Lead, Halo Analytics
Aisha.Khan@haloanalytics.com

On another note, can you confirm whether Redwood keeps KV cache logs for evaluation purposes? We want to ensure we can reproduce replies from the demo.
', 'From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@haloanalytics.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-05T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Halo POC — recommended shortlist & hands-on eval blueprint

Hi Aisha / Sofia —

Quick answers to the items Aisha flagged:  
- QA regression checklist: included in the Drive bundle (see "quality_guardrails.md" inside the eval pack). Short version: token-level precision/recall on labeled intents, hallucination heuristic (named-entity hallucination rate), and policy-safe output checks. We’ll provide per-candidate regression deltas after the sweep.
- Cost delta table: attached in latency_cost_matrix_q2.xlsx; we’ll add a 95th percentile column and publish updated numbers by tomorrow morning. Early signal from our microbench: Candidate B reduces 95th pct latency by ~35% vs baseline on g4-reserve but increases token cost by ~18% in fp16 runs. Candidate A is the best cost winner under steady throughput batching.
- KV cache logs: Redwood can enable KV cache tracing in the sandbox for the duration of the eval; logs are ephemeral for the test window and we can export anonymized traces for reproducibility. Confirm if you want those on — we’ll need a quick access form filled by Tomas.

I’ll also drop a link to a short notebook we use for the regression sweep (perf + quality).

Ben
Ben Carter | Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: quality_guardrails.md (doc), perf_regression_notebook.ipynb (notebook)
', 'From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@haloanalytics.com>, Tomas Oliveira <tomas@haloanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-06T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Halo POC — recommended shortlist & hands-on eval blueprint

Perfect — thanks for the confirmations, Aisha and Tomas. Two operational next steps from our side:

1) Calendar & kickoff: I’m sending a 30-minute kickoff for Monday 2028-06-10 09:00 PT (invite sent). Please accept and include any additional Halo engineers who will touch the sandbox.

2) Access form: Tomas — could you fill the short infra access form we use (link included in Drive). Once we have service account details we’ll provision the sandbox and enable KV-trace mode (as Ben noted).

Ben / Marissa: can you prioritize adding the 95th percentile numbers to the cost/latency sheet and post the perf notebook in the Drive folder before kickoff? Aisha: we’ll run the regression checklist during days 4–8 and will flag any hallucination spikes immediately.

If there are no objections, we’ll treat Candidate A as the default cost-optimized path for the first sprint and Candidate B as the low-latency fallback. Candidate C will remain available for long-context verification runs. We’ll capture the final decision in the mutual_action_plan_halo.docx at the end of the eval.

Thanks — looking forward to the sprint.
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova | Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai

Attachment pointers: mutual_action_plan_halo.docx (template); Drive: https://drive.example.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-halo-eval-pack']
